---
title: "Installation"
---

## Requirements

- Linux, Python ≥ 3.11.
- [Quarto](https://quarto.org) to render reports (PDF through Typst, bundled with Quarto, or
  LaTeX/TinyTeX).
- A terminal text editor for scripts: `nano` (default) or `vi`.
- For the AI assistant: an API key (Claude, ChatGPT) or a local [Ollama](https://ollama.com)
  server.
- For the web interface: a recent browser (Firefox, Chrome or Edge ≥ 121, Safari ≥ 17.2).
- Or nothing at all: the AppImage (below) contains Python, onthesignal and its web engine.

## Install

```bash
cd onthesignal
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e .            # core
.venv/bin/pip install -e ".[ai]"      # + AI providers (anthropic, openai, ollama)
.venv/bin/pip install -e ".[web]"     # + web interface (NiceGUI 4, Jedi, ruff): onthesignal web
.venv/bin/pip install -e ".[desktop]" # + its own window (PySide6, Qt WebEngine): onthesignal desktop
.venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev,docs]" # + tests and documentation tools
```

The `onthesignal` command is then available in `.venv/bin/`.

## First launch

```bash
.venv/bin/onthesignal                     # empty console
.venv/bin/onthesignal data/*.mseed        # console with files loaded as S1, S2...
.venv/bin/onthesignal --version
.venv/bin/onthesignal web                 # web interface on http://127.0.0.1:8080
.venv/bin/onthesignal desktop             # the same in its own window, like an application
```

Type `/` to open the command menu, `/help` for the list, `/quit` (or Ctrl+D) to leave. The web
interface is described in [Web interface](web.qmd).

## AppImage

The AppImage is a single file that runs on Linux without installing anything: it contains
Python, onthesignal with its web, AI and desktop dependencies, and the Chromium engine of Qt
WebEngine. It opens the web interface in its own window (`onthesignal desktop`).

```bash
chmod +x onthesignal-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage
./onthesignal-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage                    # window; asks for the project folder
./onthesignal-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage --project ~/bench3 data/*.mseed
./onthesignal-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage --console          # the console
./onthesignal-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage web --port 8090    # the server only (onthesignal web)
```

Launched from the menu of applications, it proposes the last project folder; launched from a
terminal, the project is the current folder. Quarto is not included: install it to render the
reports. To build the AppImage again (about 400 MB, 600 MB downloaded):

```bash
pip install python-appimage
python packaging/appimage/build_appimage.py      # writes dist/onthesignal-<version>-x86_64.AppImage
```

| Problem | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| `Cannot mount AppImage, please check your FUSE setup` | install FUSE (`fuse3`), or run with `--appimage-extract-and-run` |
| Same message after `fusermount3: file descriptor 5 is not a socket` | the terminal belongs to an application installed as a snap (the integrated terminal of VS Code, for example): the AppArmor profile of `fusermount3` (Ubuntu 25.10 and later) refuses it. Launch the AppImage from the menu of applications, the file manager or another terminal, or with `--appimage-extract-and-run` |
| The window stays blank | the sandbox of Chromium is refused by the system: `QTWEBENGINE_DISABLE_SANDBOX=1 ./onthesignal-…AppImage` |
| Messages of the server | `.onthesignal/logs/desktop-server.log` in the project |
